theorem: At every strict overshoot edge P--Q with q(P)<r^2<q(Q), the exact algebraic arc has a unique interior crossing point on that edge because q is continuous and strictly monotone on the oriented edge.
That crossing belongs to every native triangular cell incident to the crossed edge. Away from sector boundaries this is exactly two cells; all are legitimate shell hits.

PRE/DOWN replaces the shell point by P, POST/UP replaces it by Q, and NEAREST_SQUARED_NORM replaces it by whichever endpoint has smaller q-deficit. None of these substitutions is the exact shell-to-cell incidence map.
Nearest ties occur on some diagonal edges, but even a non-tied nearest endpoint can be noncanonical: at r=2 nearest selects POST while the exact shell crosses the edge at (sqrt(3),1) or (1,sqrt(3)).

Therefore q arithmetic alone does not select a canonical endpoint collapse direction. The canonical local geometric object presently justified is the set-valued incident-cell hit of the exact algebraic edge crossing.
continuity: Exact incidence preserves sector arc continuity automatically. Proxy endpoint substitution can mark cells not intersected by q=r^2 and therefore may alter trace history; such over-tracing is not allowed to override incidence.
reverse_path_firewall: Minimum-jump distance to PRE/POST vertices is secondary provenance and cannot choose the vector-radius shell or collapse direction.
scope: single chamber/sector; global chamber gluing remains AT4-main work
